aspects.says: A constant with a body is an instance of an anonymous subclass, so getClass() is not the enum for it; getDeclaringClass() is, and switch, EnumSet and EnumMap are unaffected.
basis: section:A Constant With a Body Is an Anonymous Subclass, So getClass() Isn't the Enum

aspects.says: An enum can't extend a class, because it already extends java.lang.Enum, and no class can extend an enum: one without constant bodies is implicitly final.
basis: section:An Enum's Type Is Closed: It Can't Extend a Class, Take a Type Parameter, or Be Extended

aspects.says: An enum's constants are built before its later static fields are assigned: a constructor that reads one directly doesn't compile, and one that reaches it through a method fails class initialisation, after which every use throws NoClassDefFoundError.
basis: section:A Constructor Runs Before the Enum's Static Fields Are Assigned

aspects.says: JPA's @Enumerated defaults to EnumType.ORDINAL, so the name mapping has to be asked for.
basis: section:An Ordinal Is a Position, and Inserting a Constant Moves It
aspects.reason: the practice runner has no JPA provider; the ticket-store practices check the same choice without one

aspects.says: Normalising case with toUpperCase() under a Turkish default locale gives a dotted capital I that valueOf rejects; toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT) doesn't.
basis: section:valueOf Accepts Only the Exact Name and Throws on Anything Else
aspects.reason: a side trap of String case mapping shown once on the page; the ticket-store practices read names exactly as they were written, so no case mapping is involved

aspects.says: An enum can't declare a type parameter; JEP 301 proposed generic enums and was withdrawn, so Java 21 still refuses one.
basis: section:An Enum's Type Is Closed: It Can't Extend a Class, Take a Type Parameter, or Be Extended

aspects.says: A stored ordinal points at another constant once a constant is inserted, removed or reordered, so what leaves the JVM is the name (not a display toString) or a code of your own.
basis: section:An Ordinal Is a Position, and Inserting a Constant Moves It

aspects.says: valueOf accepts only the exact name, never returns null, throws IllegalArgumentException on an unknown name and NullPointerException on null, so a reader of stored names decides what an unknown one means.
basis: section:valueOf Accepts Only the Exact Name and Throws on Anything Else
